Hannah / Grace — reviewed the redline. High-level technical notes:
- Subprocessor clause: We have a small set of cloud infra providers & monitoring vendors. Full "no subprocessor without consent" is operationally risky; any consent-first flow would significantly slow down our patching and scaling (we rely on partner upgrades).
- Model-training prohibition: We have strict tenancy and opt-out controls; we can commit to contract language that prohibits using Acme production data to continue training models or for improving general model weights. However, we currently perform service-level telemetry (error rates, latency) and aggregated telemetry for product improvements; we can make that aggregated telemetry non-personal and exclude Acme identifiers.
- Audit evidence: Can provide SOC2 report and a network/data flow diagram. 30-day on-demand audit is heavy; propose instead a standard SOC2 + annual penetration test + ad-hoc audit with notice and reasonable scope/cost-sharing.

If Legal/Security want to tighten, we should propose specific exception wording that documents subprocessors list and a 30-day notice for changes.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Engineering Manager — Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com; dev_patel@redwood.com; grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines: subprocessors & data use — need Product/Security sign-off

Thanks Dev — adding Security perspective. Short answer: we cannot accept an absolute ban on subprocessors. Operationally critical partners must be allowed. Proposed guardrails we can sign up to: 
- Maintain a current subprocessors roster in the contract (annex) and notify Acme of material changes with 30 days' notice.
- Forbid using Acme production data for model re-training or for inclusion in any training corpus used to update general models (we will add explicit contractual prohibition).
- Telemetry/analytics: commitments to only collect aggregated telemetry, maintain pseudonymization, and exclude PII/Acme identifiers.
- Audit: provide SOC2 Type II report and network/data flow diagram; for deeper audits, require scope agreement and cost sharing.

I'll propose redline language to Legal. If Acme insists on prior approval for every subprocessor, we can offer a short-term commercial exception (one-time) while we onboard them, but not as a permanent policy.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA redlines: subprocessors & data use — Product/Security response and next steps

Kevin / Acme Legal — thanks for the redline and patience. Quick summary of where we stand:
1) Subprocessors: Redwood cannot accept a blanket prior-consent requirement. We will provide a detailed subprocessors annex (attached) and commit to 30-day notice of material changes. For procurement purposes, we can include a one-time right to review/raise concerns on new critical subprocessors during contract signature, not an ongoing approval veto.
2) Model training/data use: Redwood will add explicit contractual language prohibiting the use of Acme production data to train or improve general model weights. We will continue to use aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry for product health and performance improvements and will exclude Acme identifiers.
3) Audit evidence: We can provide our latest SOC2 Type II report and a dataflow/network diagram (attached). For on-demand deep-dive audits, we'll agree scope and cost-sharing.

Attached: DPA_Acme_Redline_2026-02-01.docx (redline with proposed language), DataFlowDiagram_Acme_2026-02-02.pdf

- Hannah: circulate proposed redline to Acme Legal by EOD.
- Grace (Legal): finalize contract wording for subprocessors annex and model-use prohibition.
- Rishi: confirm any additional technical attestations we can include in the contract.

If this is acceptable, we can close the procurement loop this week.
